text.p: These are the stories making headlines in the Namibian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A leaked secret cabinet document reveals that top government officials are busy preparing their multi-million Namibia dollar retirement packages while other public servants have been told there is no money for pay rises this year.

- Dr Andre Rwamakuba, a former Rwandan education minister working in the Katutura state hospital but wanted by the Rwandan government, and due to stand trial for involvement in the 1994 genocide, appears to have gone underground.
- Minister of information and broadcasting Ben Amathila has castigated the media for using an official leaked document on retirement packages for top government officials.
- The fisheries ministry has increased the quota for hake from 10,000 to 120,000 tonnes following the recovery of fish stocks off the Namibian coast.

- During a media conference following the weekly cabinet briefing on Wednesday, information minister Ben Amathila issued veiled threats to the media following the publication of a leaked document on retirement packages for top government officials.
- Cabinet on Wednesday approved a total of 138 new long-term fishing rights for various types of fish, as well as the seal quotas for the 1997 season.
